henry.title: People on the Moon, Robots at Mercury
henry.intro: About 15 minutes after the grown-up says go. Short reading, then one Mercury look. A missing cliff is a real observation. Your score is the worksheet.
setup: Open Regolith yourself. This page has no launch button. Press H before Henry drives. Follow H if it disagrees with this card. Candidate b1505a7 was not drive-tested.
Do not overwrite a save you want. Backspace may cost something. Henry uses W A S D only. You use the menus.

One landing: Mercury. Prefer a readable Discovery Rupes (lobate scarp) or Caloris Planitia (basin floor). Also readable if those are missing: Kuiper crater, Intercrater plains, Prokofiev. Do not require a cliff, bright rays, or ice. Polar frost in the sim is incomplete.
Pause the 15 minutes while you set up. Skip Titan, Io, Europa, and nameless sites. Ignore a flickering globe. If Mercury will not appear, he uses the NASA pages and writes BACKUP.
steps: 📖 Read the three short chunks. Answer the checks.
🗓️ Fill the Apollo blanks from the reading. You can tap 🔊.
👀 Look at one Mercury place. Write what you expected and what you see.
🖼️ Compare one NASA picture or sentence. Label it NASA.
links: Crew and July 1969. You already have the dates in the reading.
NASA photo: a bootprint on the Moon
People really walked there in 1969. This is a photo, not the game.
A spacecraft orbited Mercury. It was the first Mercury mission after Mariner 10.

passage.text: 🚀 NASA’s Apollo 11 crew was Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin, and Michael Collins. The Eagle landed on July 20, 1969. Armstrong stepped out first. Collins stayed in orbit.
passage.q: Who stepped on the Moon first?

passage.text: 🛰️ Mercury is a different story. NASA’s MESSENGER spacecraft orbited Mercury for more than four years. Mariner 10 flew past earlier. People have not walked on Mercury.

🪨 A round pit can be a crater from an impact. A long cliff can be a scarp. Discovery Rupes is a famous long cliff. Caloris Planitia is a wide basin. You might not see that shape. Write NOT SEEN. That counts. Little rocks in the game are model scenery, not a piece of Mercury.
passage.q: What do you write if the cliff is missing?

words: a person who travels in space
a machine that can go without a person walking there
a round pit, often from an impact
a long cliff; on Mercury, a kind called a lobate scarp
the shape you can actually see

handsOn.title: One Mercury place, then a NASA picture
steps: guides/draw-adult.svg
Grown-up. Confirm H. Open one readable Mercury name. Tell Henry the name you see, not a name that is missing.

henry.challenge: Why can a bootprint last on the Moon? NASA’s Moon fact sheet lists only a trace of air, not wind like Earth’s. Mercury’s air is also only a trace. Say that in one sentence, and label it NASA, not a game measurement.

parentKey.assess: Score the worksheet. 5 = Apollo date and Armstrong, no people on Mercury plus Mariner 10 or MESSENGER, an honest Mercury note (NOT SEEN is full credit), and a NASA comparison that does not treat game pebbles as a real sample. Reading checks are not the score.
parentKey.limits: Mercury model gravity 3.70 m/s² and essentially no air. Those are model inputs, not a gauge. Source place names are declared; seeing a scarp or rays was not tested. Do not require them. No ice promise. No E/M/Home/Shift-boost/Space as verified keys. Build not drive-tested.

items.a: Landed July 20, 1969. First out: Neil Armstrong (Buzz Aldrin also walked; Collins did not). People on Mercury: no. Mission: MESSENGER or Mariner 10. The NASA Apollo 11 page also shows launch July 16 and splashdown July 24. Those are not required on the sheet.

Credit the place name you actually opened. A proposal (crater from an impact, or scarp from squeezed crust) must be tied to a shape he saw, or he writes NOT SEEN. Absence is correct. Circle true for model scenery.

A bootprint can last because the Moon has no Earth-like wind. That is from the thin lunar atmosphere on the NASA Moon fact sheet (surface pressure at night is tiny). Do not accept “I saw no wind in the game” as the proof.

frankie.title: A Moon Print and a New World 👣
frankie.intro: Grown-up, read aloud. People left a bootprint on the Moon. Today we also look at Mercury in the game. About 14 minutes after you say go.
setup: Show the NASA bootprint photo first. Then open Regolith yourself. Press H. Frankie uses W A S D only.
One Mercury landing. Pick a readable name. You may say “Rupes” or “Caloris” only if that is the name on screen. Do not promise a cliff or ice.
If the game fails, stay with the bootprint photo and the counting you can do on that page. Write BACKUP.
steps: 👀 Look at the real bootprint photo.
🚗 Roll and stop up to 3 times. Make one mark each time.
🔢 Count round shapes you really see, up to 3.
✏️ Trace I see a pit. Write pit.
links: Grown-up: this photo is from 1969. It is not the game.

handsOn.title: Photo, then a short Mercury look
steps: guides/card-count.svg
On the photo, point to the boot mark. Say: a person made this long ago.
guides/draw-wasd.svg
In the game, roll and stop. One mark each stop. Stop by 3.
guides/card-shapes.svg
Point to round pits if you see them. The drawing is not the game. Zero pits is allowed.
guides/draw-adult.svg
Grown-up. You opened Mercury. Read the place name. He copies what you point to.
handsOn.look: A boot mark in the photo. In the game, his own tally and his own pits.
handsOn.q: Copy a name, count your marks, trace pit.

worksheet: The bootprint photo is: a real NASA photo / the game. Circle one.
Roll-and-stop marks (0 to 3): ______   Round shapes I saw (0 to 3): ______

Sound it out. Draw a line.
pit   sun   map
🗺️   🕳️   ☀️
Circle every on: A pit is on the map. I am on it.

Trace: I see a pit.
Stretch: Write pit:

parentKey.assess: Score the sheet. The photo is NASA, not the game. His tallies are right if they match what he did. There is no required pit total. pit → hole, sun → sun, map → map. Both on words. Stretch: pit.
parentKey.limits: Do not require a scarp, rays, or a fixed count. No drawing beyond tracing letters.

items.a: Circle a real NASA photo. Place word is whatever you pointed to on screen, or BACKUP if you skipped the game. Marks and pits: any 0–3 that matches him.
